entry.note: Webster-Williamson Geometry of Markov traces. DIRECT fit with QOU Markov-trace content. Cited in hecke-markov-interpretation.ts (cites array).

relevance.rationale: JOIN CONFIRMED from front matter: the document self-identifies as arXiv:0911.4494v2, matching the preprint id recorded on the registered entry, and its abstract matches the entry's subject. NOT LOAD-BEARING: the id appears only in one .ts cites array (mass-theory/hecke-markov-interpretation.ts:21) and in zero .md prose, zero .lean, zero computations. The hecke-markov-interpretation.md narrative is entirely about SYT paths, the Hoefsmit seminormal form and the Mallows-measure stochastic operator — Diaconis-Ram territory — and never invokes anything from this document. That is a reference carried in a manifest whose results the corpus never uses. Substantively it is a good fit and deserves better than a dangling cites entry: it gives a geometric construction of the Jones-Ocneanu trace on the Hecke algebra via equivariant cohomology of sheaves on SL_n, and expands that trace over the irreducible Hecke characters — structurally the same shape as the QOU Frobenius pairing tr_M = sum_lambda y_lambda chi_lambda. Two caveats keep this at supporting rather than core: the expansion is bigraded in (q,t) with weights given by mixed Poincare polynomials of character sheaves, not the single-variable y_lambda(q) QOU uses, and QOU's weights already come from the Wedderburn/Jones route, so nothing here is needed. Minor metadata mismatch for references.ts (not for this ledger): the registered entry's venue/date differ from the attached preprint version's date.

keyResults.statement: The geometric trace expands over irreducible characters as Tr(x) = sum_chi chi_q(x) * {chi, nu} * M_nu(q,t), where {chi,nu} are Lusztig Fourier-transform matrix coefficients and M_nu is the mixed Poincare polynomial of the corresponding character sheaf.
keyResults.useForFolio: An independent, geometric identification of the character weights in the Markov-trace expansion tr_M = sum_lambda y_lambda chi_lambda — a second route to the y_lambda that does not go through Wedderburn.

keyResults.statement: The trace Tr(C'_w) = dim_{q,t} H*_{B_Delta}(IC_w) depends only on the root system, and agrees with the trace defined independently by Gomi.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the well-definedness context for treating the Markov trace as a root-system-level invariant rather than a type-A accident.

proposedActions.rationale: The reference currently sits in rem:hecke-markov-interpretation's cites array with no prose invocation. Move it to the block whose claim it actually bears on — the character expansion of the Markov trace — and cite Cor. 13 there with its locator.
